years of MICAI · 2000–2026
A longitudinal analysis of institutional collaboration networks across the conference proceedings.
Building on last year’s studyMICAI and the Making of AI in Mexico through 25 Years of Data-Driven Insight (Avalos-Gauna, Palafox & Martínez-Villaseñor, 2025) traced topics, host cities and international reach. This paper asks the next question: how do institutions connect?

⚠️ Core-periphery is fragile
Peripheral institutions reach the network through the core, not through each other.
Lose core capacity (funding, faculty, participation) and the ecosystem can break into disconnected pieces.
Conceptual illustration
🧭 What could change it
Strengthen direct ties among peripheral institutions
💰
Co-fund periphery-to-periphery
Reward projects that tie peripheral institutions together, not only periphery-to-core partnerships.
🤝
Twin and mentor
Core institutions help connect peripheral ones, instead of acting as everyone’s only hub.
📊
Measure structure, not headcount
Track periphery-internal density and core-dependency next to participation.
🔍 Limits and next steps
Limits
🔭
One venue only: MICAI is a partial lens
🔤
Auto-generated acronyms can merge distinct institutions in the periphery
🤖
LLM extraction audited on a stratified sample, not on every record
Next
🌐
More venues: COMIA, Web of Science
🧭
Topic analysis alongside the turning points
🧹
Better name resolution for peripheral institutions
Nodes make a network grow.
Bridges make it mature.
